Refuse a reference bundle built by a different normalizer

Source: R/match.R
pf_check_reference.Rd

Checkpoints have carried a normalizer stamp since .pf_run_stamp(), but a fresh run against a stale REF-augmented.rds had nothing to catch it. This closes that gap, on the same principle: recomputing wastes time, reusing a mismatched key produces a result that looks correct and is not.

Usage

pf_check_reference(ref, action = c("auto", "stop", "warn", "ignore"))

Arguments

ref

A bundle from pf_build_reference(), a matchdb tier from pf_reference(), or a bare reference frame.

action

"auto" (default: stop on a mismatch, warn on a missing stamp), or force "stop", "warn" or "ignore".

Value

ref, invisibly.

Details

Two cases, deliberately different in severity. A bundle stamped with a different signature is known wrong, so "auto" stops. A bundle with no stamp is merely unknown — it predates stamping and may well be current — and a reference is 2.8 GB and hours to rebuild from the BMF, so "auto" warns rather than blocking a run that is probably fine. Checkpoints stop in both cases because recomputing one is cheap; this is the same principle applied to a much more expensive artifact.

The signature is read from either place a reference records it: normalizer on a bundle from pf_build_reference(), or stamp$normalize_signature on a matchdb tier fetched by pf_reference(). Reading only the first would report a stamped matchdb tier as unstamped and downgrade a real mismatch to a warning — and a warning nobody can act on is worse than no check.
